root_cause_correctness.evidence: Verified by direct Read of MarkdownView.tsx working-tree at lines 412-486. Lines 419-426 (WebTableRow <td>) and 444-447 (RenderTableBlockWeb <th>) place <RenderSpans/> as a direct child of raw web <td>/<th> with NO parent <Text> wrapper. Native counterpart at lines 470-473 (header) and 478-481 (cell) DOES wrap RenderSpans inside <Text style={style.tableHeaderText/tableCellText}>. RenderSpans (line 380-385) returns siblings via map of <RenderSpanItem/> each emitting <Text> (line 363). On react-native-web, an orphan <Text> not nested inside another <Text> renders as a flex/block container by default, causing each formatted span to occupy its own line. Confirmed independently by close-debate Round 2 codex + QA reassessment via desktop and mobile screenshots. style.tableHeaderText (line 801) and style.tableCellText (line 807) both exist in the StyleSheet. BA's localization is precise.

min_scope_fix.sufficiency: Wrapping RenderSpans in a single parent <Text style={style.tableCellText|tableHeaderText}> establishes the RNW Text-context that nests sibling <Text> spans inline. This pattern is already proven correct by the native path (lines 470, 478) and by the same file's other inline-rendering call sites (lines 163, 169, 178, 213) which all wrap RenderSpans in a parent <Text> with baseStyle propagation. The fix is structurally identical to the working pattern, so sufficiency follows by symmetry.
min_scope_fix.necessity: An alternative — applying display:inline via CSS to the inner Text — would require RNW-only styling that bypasses the cross-platform abstraction and would not match the native path. The proposed wrapper-<Text> reuses the existing project-internal correct pattern with zero new abstractions. No cheaper alternative exists that preserves cross-platform parity.
min_scope_fix.side_effects: Examined and acceptable. (1) Link tap-targets: each <a>/Pressable is rendered individually inside RenderSpanItem (line 371), unchanged by an outer <Text> — taps remain on the per-span elements. (2) Accessibility tree: one additional grouping <Text> node is added; this matches the native path which already does so. (3) RTL layout: <Text> defers to RNW's text-direction inheritance — no change. (4) Existing `?? ''` empty-cell guards (lines 424, 479) preserved per BA's pre_existing_guards declaration with removal_authorized=false. (5) baseStyle propagation through RenderSpans (line 363) applies the wrapper's style to inner spans, matching native behavior. No CSS-inheritance regression risk for selectable / fontFamily / link styling because all are explicitly set per-span via styleMap.

ac_measurability.ac_new_1: ±2px tolerance on getBoundingClientRect().y is tight enough to catch a regression (block-stacking would produce y-deltas of one full line-height ~16-24px) yet loose enough to absorb sub-pixel font-metric rounding. Both viewports (desktop 1440x900, mobile 390x844) explicitly specified. Playwright MCP + getBoundingClientRect both available in the dev environment per Cycle 1 QA's already-captured trace evidence. Recipe acknowledges natural text-wrapping relaxation when cell content overflows cell width — sensible. Minor nit (not blocking): the example selector queries `[style*='font-weight: 700']` may need adapting at execution time to RNW's inline-style serialization; QA can compensate with computed-style queries — the maxYDelta assertion is the load-bearing check and is selector-agnostic.
ac_measurability.ac_new_2: Cycle 1's parseMarkdown.test.ts (7/7 pass) is parser-level and inadequate alone for catching a layout regression in the wrapper change, but combined with the bounding-rect measurement of AC-NEW-1 + Cycle 1's role/href/fontWeight DOM measurements (which would catch any accidental link-target or styling break), coverage is sufficient. The full Vitest 460/57-skipped baseline guards against unrelated breakages. AC-NEW-2 does not require additional bounding-rect assertions on existing fixtures because those fixtures render outside tables and are unaffected by the wrapper change scoped strictly to <td>/<th>.
